subject: ILCE-6400 CXD90045 transition, boot-mode, and persistent-updater boundary

observations.source: signed Windows transfer engine FUN_004012d0, FUN_00401f40, FUN_00406900, FUN_00406a70, and FUN_004061c0
observations.claim: The host parses the DAT container, reads bytes directly from the FDAT extent, and copies them into command-0x0040 packets before command 0x0100. No host transform appears in the complete read-to-send path, and the alpha 6400 v2.00 and alpha 7 III v4.00 packages contain the same 122864-byte signed engine.

observations.source: offline historical fwtool decode and validated DAT geometry
observations.claim: The alpha 6400 v2.00, alpha 7 III v4.00, and alpha 7 III v4.01 payloads all validate as CXD90045 generation-four packages with a 0x110-byte outer trailer and independently decoded inner firmware layouts.

observations.source: byte-identical partinf.conf and up.sh in alpha 6400 v2.00 and alpha 7 III v4.00/v4.01
observations.claim: The common partition map labels /dev/nflasha1 as an 8323072-byte updater system partition. Each examined payload carries images only for nflasha3, nflasha5, nflasha7, and nflasha15, so no examined package replaces nflasha1.

up.sh selects updater-related modes by creating files under /setting/updater and passes a numeric mode argument to ud_send_lsi.elf. That utility places the numeric argument in an OSAL message and waits for a response; it contains no partition mount or firmware transform in its main path.

observations.source: normal /sbin/init check_bootmode decompilation and mount table
observations.claim: Normal init reads /proc/udm/upm_bootmode only to recognize USB_CHARGE, ADJUST, and BIS flags. Its static mount table does not mount /dev/nflasha1, placing selection of the updater system before this normal userspace path.

observations.source: alpha 7 III v4.00/v4.01 runtime hashes and alpha 6400/alpha 7 III secure-program hashes
observations.claim: The alpha 7 III v4.00 and v4.01 crypter, UFP, and talk libraries are byte-identical across releases, while the registered AES/SHA2 and UDRT secure programs are also byte-identical to the alpha 6400 copies. The visible crypter paths remain raw-file ingress followed by blockwise Dec_Scramble ECB.

inferences.source: persistent updater partition omitted from three decoded packages plus pre-userspace mode selection
inferences.claim: The permanent updater system or the loader that selects it is now the primary missing software boundary for the generation-four CBC and authenticity checks. This replaces the earlier assumption that a per-release transition receiver had to be embedded in the target partitions.

inferences.source: raw host transfer, raw visible receiver path, ECB-only crypter, and absent updater-partition image
inferences.claim: The unresolved CBC and authenticity implementation could reside on /dev/nflasha1, in an earlier loader, or behind a hardware or secure-execution interface. The current static evidence does not distinguish those locations.

inferences.source: byte-identical registered secure programs across models
inferences.claim: The shared secure-program hashes are compatible with a common service boundary, but identity alone does not prove that either program performs firmware CBC processing or signature verification.

unresolved.claim: No authentic /dev/nflasha1 image or equivalent updater-system dump has been acquired, so its executables, libraries, and configuration remain unavailable for static analysis.
The exact component that converts the /setting/updater mode files and LSI message into updater-partition boot selection has not been located.
The CBC implementation, signature verifier, signed byte range, failure mapping, and public trust anchor remain unlocated.
No safe method to authorize a model-mismatched package, reproduce Sony authenticity metadata, or build an installable alpha 6400 image has been established.

conclusion: The raw host transfer and visible Linux receiver/crypter path are now reconciled by a persistent updater-system boundary: /dev/nflasha1 is explicitly labeled as the updater partition, selected before normal userspace, and omitted from all three decoded CXD90045 payloads examined. This is a materially narrower target for future static work, but its contents and the earlier loader remain missing, so the CBC implementation, signature verifier, trust anchor, bypass, and any installable alpha 6400 package are still unproven.
